items.stem: A page loads a large render-blocking stylesheet in the head before any content paints. What is the most direct improvement?

options.text: Reduce and prioritise critical CSS so rendering is not blocked by non-critical styles
options.rationale: Correct: delivering only critical CSS first unblocks the first paint while the rest loads non-blocking.

options.text: Add a second copy of the stylesheet
options.rationale: Duplicating the stylesheet adds bytes and does not unblock rendering.

options.text: Convert the CSS to a large inline image
options.rationale: An image cannot replace stylesheet rules and would add weight.

options.text: Ignore it because CSS never affects load time
options.rationale: Render-blocking CSS directly delays first paint.

items.explanation: Correct: delivering only critical CSS first unblocks the first paint while the rest loads non-blocking.

items.stem: Which TWO techniques reduce the amount of JavaScript executed on initial load? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Code splitting so non-critical code loads on demand
options.rationale: Correct: splitting defers code until it is needed, shrinking the initial payload.

options.text: Tree shaking to drop unused exports from the bundle
options.rationale: Correct: tree shaking removes dead code from the shipped bundle.

options.text: Inlining every dependency into one large bundle
options.rationale: One large bundle increases, not reduces, initial JavaScript.

options.text: Running all analytics synchronously at startup
options.rationale: Synchronous startup work adds main-thread cost, worsening load.

items.explanation: Correct: splitting defers code until it is needed, shrinking the initial payload.

items.stem: Before optimising, what should guide which fixes to make first?

options.text: Measurement showing where time is actually spent, ranked by impact
options.rationale: Correct: measuring first ensures effort targets the real bottlenecks.

options.text: Guessing based on which code looks oldest
options.rationale: Code age is not evidence of a performance bottleneck.

options.text: Optimising the smallest files first for quick wins
options.rationale: Small files are rarely the bottleneck; impact should drive order.

options.text: Changing everything at once without measuring
options.rationale: Changing everything blindly makes impact impossible to attribute.

items.explanation: Correct: measuring first ensures effort targets the real bottlenecks.
